atomicity.reason: One obligation (flag implausible cell voltage samples); the median computation is the means to that decision rather than a separate deliverable, and the complement sentence closes the same rule.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: the scope, the statistic, the threshold and both flag outcomes are all stated in the requirement.

feasibility.reason: A per-module median over a handful of samples every 10 ms is well within budget and contradicts nothing else stated.

parent_fit.reason: ARCH_CELL_MEASUREMENT_ACQ owns the plausibility decision - per-module median of cell voltages, marking any cell deviating by more than 250 mV as invalid - and this requirement states exactly that.

unambiguity.reason: 'the median' is not defined for a module with an even number of cells, where the mean of the two central samples and the lower central sample give different results and therefore different flags near the boundary.
unambiguity.suggestion: Define the median for even cell counts, e.g. 'the arithmetic mean of the two central values when the module has an even number of cells'.

verifiability.reason: The 250 mV threshold, the absolute-difference comparison, the 'exceeds' boundary and the per-module per-cycle scope let a test assert flags for a constructed sample set.

summary: Tight refinement of the parent's plausibility rule with the complement stated explicitly; only the definition of 'median' for an even cell count is left open.
